questions.q: Why generate the numbers in a model card from code instead of typing them in?
options: It is required by scikit-learn
It makes the model more accurate
The card stays in sync with the actual run and cannot drift or contain typos
Markdown cannot contain numbers typed by hand
questions.explain: Filling a template from the run's own results means the documented metrics, seed, and versions are exactly what produced the model.

questions.q: What is a data fingerprint, as used in the lesson's model card?
options: A short hash of the dataset, so two people can check they are using the same data
The name of the person who owns the data
A list of the column names
A picture of the data distribution
questions.explain: The lesson hashes the CSV form of the data with SHA-256 and keeps the first 12 characters. A different fingerprint means different data.

questions.q: Which limitation is the best one to put in a model card?
options: Results may vary
The model is not perfect
Use with caution
Trained on one region only; recall for new customers is unknown; 0.5 threshold misses most churners
questions.explain: Good limitations are specific and checkable. Vague statements give a reader nothing to act on.

questions.q: A saved model file (joblib) should be stored with a note of which library version?
options: The scikit-learn version, because saved models are tied to it
Only the operating system version
None; joblib files work with any version
The version of your text editor
questions.explain: Pickled scikit-learn models can fail or behave differently when loaded under another scikit-learn version, so record the version beside the file.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a decisions log entry such as 'Chose logistic regression over random forest'?
options: To replace the README
To record the reason at the time, so future readers know why and when to revisit
To store the trained model
To list every hyperparameter tried
questions.explain: A dated entry with context, the decision, the why, and a revisit trigger preserves reasoning that would otherwise be forgotten.
